summary: Sticky routing / affinity failure causing repeated connection resets for KelpGuard enterprise during canary spike
description:
Issue summary: KelpGuard reported large numbers of connection resets and truncated streaming responses during a scheduled canary for a custom routing policy. Impact: customer-facing calls returned repeated short-lived connections and ~25% duplicate reconnects leading to degraded transcript completeness for policy inference. Environment: production, us-west-2, customer pinned to dedicated routing policy and enterprise plan.

Observed impact window: 2026-03-11 02:40-03:15 UTC. Customer reported escalations to Redwood Support and SRE due to elevated error rates and user-visible truncations.

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Send continuous streaming requests with routing header X-RW-Routing: kelpguard-canary to us-west endpoint.
2) Observe that initial socket connects then resets after 1-3s.
3) Subsequent retries frequently hit a different backend that drops the KV cache leading to partial transcripts.

Logs: Gateway logs show 502/GRPC_CANCELLED on stream tear, routing service logs show affinity token mismatch, serving-runtime reports cache-miss spikes and rapid VM handoffs.
investigation_notes:
Timeline: 02:42 UTC support acknowledged, 02:50 SRE triaged, 02:55 Canary was paused. Hypothesis: new sticky-routing change deployed in canary routing service introduced a race between affinity assignment and backend selection under bursty connect patterns. Evidence: correlation between routing-service commit deploy at 02:33 and error spike at 02:40; rejected affinity tokens seen in routing trace logs; serving-runtime metric 'kv_cache_invalidation_rate' increased by 12x. Reproduced in isolated canary by replaying 200 RPS with short-lived client connections. Noise from autoscaler: rapid pod churn in dedicated pool contributed to lost affinity mappings.

Cross-references: linked SRE slack thread #incidents and PRs above. Engineering noted two recent commits that changed cookie expiry and fallback ordering in router.
comments: 2026-03-11 02:45 - Ivy Chen (Support): Customer reported truncated streaming transcripts and repeated reconnects; provided request IDs and sample transcripts.
2026-03-11 02:50 - SRE Triage (Jamal Ortiz): Observed GRPC_CANCELLED spikes and affinity rejections in router logs; initiating immediate rollback of canary routing change.
2026-03-11 02:55 - Marco Ruiz (Oncall Eng): Rolled back routing-service canary at 02:56 UTC; error rate began degrading toward baseline by 03:05 UTC. Notified customer of mitigation.
2026-03-11 03:10 - KelpGuard (Customer): Confirmed reduced reconnects and improved transcript completion; requested root-cause and permanent fix timeline.
2026-03-12 09:20 - Marco Ruiz (Eng): Performed deeper analysis; root cause points to race when affinity token was written but not yet visible to the routing lookup cache during rapid backend churn.
2026-03-12 14:05 - Product (Anika Patel): Agreed on safety gates for future sticky-routing changes and stricter canary load patterns; requested post-incident action items.
2026-03-13 11:30 - Ivy Chen (Support): Sent formal post-incident note and SLA credit offer to KelpGuard; scheduled follow-up call for 2026-03-16.
2026-03-13 15:00 - Marco Ruiz (Eng): Marking incident resolved; follow-up deploy plan created and merged (see PR 5879).
resolution_notes: Immediate mitigation: rolled back the routing-service canary (02:56 UTC) which returned affinity behavior to stable. Temporary customer workaround: switched KelpGuard to the conservative routing policy and increased connection hold time to reduce short-lived reconnect patterns. Permanent fix: patch in PR github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/5879 addresses race by ensuring atomic affinity write-read barrier and introducing a short grace TTL for affinity tokens on backend handoff. Patch also adds a canary load pattern guard to avoid rapid connect bursts during canary windows. Deployed to staging 2026-03-12 and scheduled production rollout 2026-03-18 behind a throttled canary ramp.
root_cause: Race condition in new sticky-routing implementation combined with rapid pod churn from aggressive autoscaler policy. Affinity tokens could be accepted by the assignment path before route lookup caches had replicated the mapping, causing subsequent requests to land on backends that did not have the expected KV prefix and leading to stream resets and truncated outputs.
postincident_action_items: Add canary load pattern guard: prevent >50 RPS short-lived connect bursts during routing canaries
Introduce atomic write-read barrier for affinity assignments (PR 5879) and add unit+integration tests
Tune autoscaler stabilization window for dedicated pools to reduce rapid pod churn during canaries
Create runbook entry for Support to toggle conservative routing policy during high-risk canaries
Schedule 1:1 with KelpGuard engineering to review change control and acceptance criteria (target week of 2026-03-16)
